When my laptop boots my headphones volume is set to 0%, I have an asus laptop that for some reason it's speaker is seen as a headphone.

I made a script that is basically 

amixer Headphones set 100%

I'm on my other computer so I can't remember if set comes before headphones or not, but I can run that script and it will work.

How would I set it up so that it runs on startup?

Edit: got it to work, thank you everyone.
How do you get a bash script to run on startup (ubuntu15.10)
One way is to put that line in your /etc/init.d/rc.local file.
You could put the line in ~/.bashrc, but have you tried running alsamixer and disabling auto-mute?

I would add it to the ~/.bash_profile file.

If you put it in ~/.bashrc it will run every time you login as well as every time you open a terminal window. But your ~/.bash_profile will only run every time you login.

This means that it goes to 100% every time you login, but won't surprise you during boot when you think you have your machine muted, but open a terminal and end up having it max itself out.
